title: Anaphylaxis in the Emergency Department
scenario: A 24-year-old male presents to the emergency department 15 minutes after eating a peanut-containing snack, reporting sudden throat tightness, difficulty breathing, and a spreading itchy rash.

lines: 24-year-old male brought to triage by a friend after eating a peanut-containing snack ~15 minutes ago. Reports throat tightness, difficulty swallowing, and shortness of breath. Diffuse urticaria over face, neck, and trunk. Lips and periorbital area swollen. Audible inspiratory stridor. Anxious and restless. Reports a known peanut allergy but no epinephrine auto-injector on hand.
Placed on cardiac monitor and continuous pulse oximetry. High-flow oxygen applied via non-rebreather mask. Two large-bore IV lines established. Provider notified and at bedside.
Epinephrine 0.3 mg (0.3 mL of 1 mg/mL) administered IM to the lateral thigh per order. Normal saline bolus infusing wide open. Client kept supine with legs elevated.
Stridor resolved and urticaria fading. Reports breathing is much easier and throat tightness improving. Remains on continuous monitoring for possible biphasic reaction.
Known allergy: peanuts (prior lip swelling and hives).
Epinephrine 0.3 mg IM now, may repeat every 5-15 minutes as needed
High-flow oxygen via non-rebreather mask, titrate to SpO2 >= 94%
Normal saline 1-2 L IV bolus for hypotension
Continuous cardiac and pulse-oximetry monitoring; observe for biphasic reaction

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Stridor, hypoxia, hypotension, and airway edema are hallmarks of a life-threatening anaphylactic reaction and demand immediate intervention. A normal temperature and WBC are not urgent.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify which body system it reflects. Each finding may reflect more than one system.
children.rationale: Stridor is airway/respiratory; hypotension and tachycardia reflect distributive shock (cardiovascular). Hypoxia with an elevated lactate reflects both impaired oxygenation and poor tissue perfusion.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the most urgent action is to {2}.
children.rationale: The immediate threat in anaphylaxis is airway compromise from laryngeal edema, and IM epinephrine is the first-line, life-saving intervention that reverses airway swelling and hypotension.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Place the client upright in high Fowler's for hypotension
Delay treatment to complete allergy testing first

children.rationale: Epinephrine, oxygen, and IV fluids treat anaphylactic shock. A hypotensive client should be kept supine with legs elevated, not upright, and treatment must never be delayed for testing.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After the first dose of IM epinephrine, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Continue continuous cardiac and pulse-oximetry monitoring
Prepare to repeat epinephrine in 5-15 minutes if symptoms persist
Administer the ordered IV antihistamine and corticosteroid as adjuncts
Continue the normal saline bolus for hypotension
Discharge the client home immediately once the rash fades
Withhold oxygen to avoid oxygen toxicity

children.rationale: After epinephrine the nurse maintains monitoring, is ready to redose, gives adjunct antihistamines and steroids, and continues fluids. Early discharge risks a biphasic reaction and oxygen should not be withheld.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.
children.rationale: Resolution of stridor, normalized blood pressure and oxygenation, and fading hives show the reaction is reversing. A rising respiratory rate would indicate worsening respiratory distress, not improvement.
